A1.justification: Both PDFs describe X-SG2S and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures supporting a reliable comparison. Inspection includes v1's Appendix A. V2 has no separate appendix; some earlier qualitative examples reappear in its main-text figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original multimodal and single-modality watermarking experiments, interaction-block and loss ablations, and payload-size analyses in Tables 1–4 and Figure 5, with qualitative results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 reports original watermarking and ablation results in Tables 1–3, pruning results in Table 4, unwatermarked-scene results in Table 5, and qualitative fidelity analyses.

M1.justification: V2 introduces feature-sparse DCAE image encoding and recovery, using redundant features, missing-patch simulation, positional recovery and refinement (Section 3.5). It also introduces repeated-binary recovery and restricts embedding to SH orders 3 and 4 (Section 3.8). These substantially revise encoding and recovery while retaining the gates and injection/extraction heads.

E1.justification: ACID scenes, Logo-2K images, Objaverse/Gamba objects and generated binary messages remain the data coverage. V2 adds evaluation on randomly pruned Gaussian clouds and watermark identification on unwatermarked scenes (Sections 4.6–4.7), extending input conditions and detection scenarios without adding datasets or domains.

E2.justification: The five interaction-block comparators remain, with Multiply/Add/Concatenate renamed Multiplication/Addition/Concatenation. V2 adds an all-SH comparator against higher-order-only embedding in Figure 7 and removes the explicit joint-versus-individual-training comparison in v1 Table 3. Newly discussed external watermarking methods are not empirically compared.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 changes the reported binary configuration from 8bit×128 to 48bit×1024, image patches from 16×32768 to 16×2048, and embedding parameters from 75 SH values to 48 higher-order values per point. V2 also introduces 5–25% random-pruning tests and unwatermarked controls. Dataset splits, rendering resolutions and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds SH-order fidelity comparisons, amplified residual maps, pruning robustness tests and unwatermarked-scene analysis (Figures 7–8, Tables 4–5). It removes v1's joint-versus-individual-training analysis and binary bit-width/message-length sweeps (Table 3, Section 4.4.4 and Figure 5). Interaction-block and optional-loss ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, independent-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's random pruning and negative-control sampling do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Many retained results are replaced: Table 1's preferred gate has scene/image PSNR 25.341/36.0062 in v1 versus 27.666/30.537 in v2, under revised method and payload settings. New Table 4 reports binary precision 1.0 through 25% pruning; Table 5 reports 0.395 on unwatermarked scenes. V1's joint-versus-individual and payload-sweep results disappear. These changes do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The Gaussian rendering equations, attention and score formulations, linear-complexity argument and overall watermarking loss remain mathematically unchanged. The new DCAE and SH discussions describe algorithmic design and intuition without adding formal assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The unified simultaneous 1D–3D watermarking claim remains. V2 adds image restoration from missing features as an explicit contribution, and its abstract and introduction newly emphasize robustness against model degradation and correct watermark judgments. This substantially expands the claimed capabilities beyond the original embedding and extraction account.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting redundancy to recovery and higher-order SH embedding to reduced visual disturbance. It interprets the new controls as demonstrating robustness and reduced false positives without a discriminator. V1's discussion of increasing message length degrading scene fidelity and its joint-versus-individual-training interpretation are removed.

D1.justification: V2 documents the DCAE's 4×4×128 latent representation, four upsampling layers and positional recovery, and changes the stated GPU from A6000ada to RTX4090. It removes the project URL and detailed Hilbert-sorting description, although references to sorted points remain. Removal of the URL does not establish that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: V2 adds references to DCAE, Splats in Splats, GaussianMarker, Stable Signature and Safe-SD. Its introduction and related work add contrasts concerning full-scene data requirements, per-scene autoencoder training and GaussianMarker's 48-bit capacity. The central positioning around unified multimodal watermarking remains.

P1.justification: Much wording and the main section sequence remain unchanged. Local revisions update the abstract and introduction, shorten the training explanation, revise method and experiment subsections, and bring qualitative material into the main text. The author list adds Liqiang Nie. These are localized editorial and structural changes rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: V2 adopts an ACM-style layout, redraws the pipeline and interaction diagrams, separates the gate illustration, and adds DCAE, redundancy, fidelity and residual displays. It removes the payload-sweep figure and joint-versus-individual table and adds pruning and negative-control tables. Some v1 appendix examples are reused within reorganized main-text qualitative figures.

improvement.justification: V2's recovery mechanism, pruning tests and SH-fidelity comparison provide useful evidence addressing v1's lack of degradation evaluation. The improvement is limited: watermark identification is claimed without a detection threshold or false-positive-rate evaluation, payload-capacity and joint-versus-individual analyses disappear, and the project link is removed. The added practical evidence modestly strengthens the paper despite these losses.
